The network measures packet arrival timing, requiring each registered node to emit steady traffic shapes that map onto a geographic atlas of validation relays. If an actor spawns thousands of puppet instances, their transmission waves collide, creating an artificial plume of dropped packets that trips local rate limits. Attackers pay a compounding latency penalty: every concurrent fake identity increases processing delays linearly, forcing them to waste significant computational power maintaining desynchronized timers across the river of incoming data streams.
